findings_nonblocking: On every one of its 68 mismatches, v2@e0b6d80 equals this oracle's pow-squaring + F3-off mutant (same ids, same mismatch strings), and it is bit-exact everywhere else. That covers the 37 new F3 fixtures, 17 boundary cases and 13 near-undefined cases.

Severity illustration: at e0b6d80, all-degenerate negative-mean cells ([-0.2,-0.1]*6, T ~ -1.32e16) reach REJECT_H0 under the one-sided GREATER test, and S1 reaches STAT_PASS. Literal run() returns a p on all 37 F3 fixtures. v1 returns a p on 33 and raises ZeroDivisionError on the 4 subnormal ones.

Periodic decimal-zero-mean series are always UNDEFINED_SE in float: 216 digit triples and 22,415 random patterns, all with se == 0. So no B=19 zero-mean F3 fixture can be built that way. The zero-mean F3 coverage uses exact binary zero mean (T == 0) with B 1-4, which are seed-lucky cases.

The 4 subnormal-underflow F3 fixtures are all-degenerate only under the mandated float predicate (v > 0 but fl(v/n) == 0). Exact arithmetic and a `v > 0` predicate call some replicates non-degenerate. An implementation that uses exact or v>0 degeneracy would miss F3 there (vpos mutant 4/37; exact-predicate mutant misses 11).

At the head's fixture parameters (n12, L2, B19, seed 7) a registry cell with deg == B-1 cannot be constructed: n12/L2 defect series stay below 0.5 per-replicate degeneracy. So an over-broad F3 rule (deg >= B-1) is detectable only by the kernel compare (17/17), not by the registry probe.

If Codex implements F3 only in the registry (kernel still returns p), compare_cdr012 reports F3_MISSING_PRODUCED_P 37 while the registry probe passes. The README instructs recording kernel FAIL and registry PASS separately and routing the difference, without merging them into one PASS.
Triage labels such as EPSILON_GUARD_SUSPECT and F3_OVERBROAD are heuristic hints only; grading is exact. The registry probe output for shim 'none' is byte-identical to the plain run (determinism).

Overall: the prep batch is sound and correctly scoped to CDR-012, but its blockers are out of date, the successor harness needs three fixes before a real run, and the RIG audit missed that MAC-X1 also blocks merging #21 in any order.

**What changed since the prep.** Codex pushed: #31 is now c9e0fa7 (CDR-012 HANDOFF_READY, GCH-010a, 9/9 CI green) and #35 is now 4cf8ead (merges c9e0fa7, STACKED, 8/8 green). So every "B1: waiting for Codex" blocker in the three reports is out of date.

**CDR-012 expectation set: complete and correctly scoped.**
- F3 applies only when deg == B. deg == B-1 keeps a p (17 cases), and near-undefined cases keep a p (14).
- No epsilon is added anywhere; the epsilon mutants are caught.
- The F1 detectors flip p between d*d and pow (16 of 16 caught at the old head e0b6d80), but only because this glibc's pow is inexact. The AST scan is the platform-independent check.
- The registry probe is meaningful. Its S2 gate-level NOT_RUN comes from the owner's unchanged v1 aggregation (any NOT_RUN cell makes the gate NOT_RUN), so it adds no new rule.
- Spot-check 1, run against c9e0fa7 itself (not the authoritative verification):
  - compare_cdr012: rc 0, EXACT_MATCH_ALL_GRADED on 747 cases, also with a strict F3 reason regex.
  - Registry probe: rc 0 (S1 NOT_RUN, S2 NOT_RUN, S3 STAT_PASS).
  - Source: d*d squaring, and the refusal is raised iff degenerate == replicates.
- Minor coverage gaps:
  - The 5 UNDEFINED_SE cases are ungraded.
  - METHOD and POLICY are unchanged even though the bits changed; only the arithmetic_contract and the supplement pin mark the change.
  - The feasibility path is not covered.

**Successor harness: fails closed where it must, but is weaker in three places.**
- Holds: VERIFIED_V2_COMMIT is required, unreviewed additions FAIL, an unchanged tree is reported NO_NEW_CONTENT with exit 3, and escalation hits give REVIEW_REQUIRED. Spot-check 2 on the real heads: STACKED topology, clean merge-trees, and a 38-file delta.
- Expected non-PASS outcomes, by design:
  - protected_paths FAILs with the default 11-entry allowlist, because the CI-declared list is now 13.
  - The CI-parity check needs review: the readiness step was renamed and its protected-paths predicate gained 2 paths.
  - The escalation sweep finds 4 benign hits that are not negated.
  - So the expected result is exit 4, not 0.
- Weaknesses:
  - VERIFIED_V2_COMMIT is only checked for ancestry, so if #31 moves on after verification, files outside the allowlist go unchecked.
  - The oracle step checks only the verdict: no registry probe, no strict reason regex, PASS on rc 0 even without JSON, and no hash pins.
  - The negation heuristic is permissive: any hit inside a one-line JSON/XML file is treated as negated.

**RIG audit: verdict sound after verification, with one more correction.**
- READY_AFTER_OWNER_ACTIONS is upheld together with the verifier's corrections.
- Spot-check 3 refutes "#21 independent, any position". Track C's boundary_audit passes with canonical at b8e39a2. With canonical at f1b5afb (#21 merged) it fails "canonical advanced". On Track C plus #21 it fails "new file outside authorized Track C" (CLAUDE.md and the contract doc).
